# Defaults for interactive use; must mirror the YAML header above.

# Overview

Two bar plots: GC% and GC3% of each **part** on its own - the (GGGGS)x3 linker,
the 1xFLAG tag and each recoded eGFP copy - rather than of the assembled
constructs. Every other notebook in this folder reports whole constructs, where
the fixed HiBiT/P2A backbone and the Waldo linkers are mixed in. This is the
per-part view, which is what goes into a synthesis order.

Each part is shown **before and after recoding**, against the MDA-MB-231
expressed median as a reference line, because the single number by itself does
not say whether it is on target. For the GS linker "before" means the naive
encoding - most-used codon per residue - since it has no native sequence; that
is the same definition `08_` and `10_` use, through the shared
`naive_encoding()`.

**Two of the five parts cannot be on target, for reasons their own amino acids
impose, and the plots are mainly a way of reading that.** Glycine and serine
are GG- and TC-/AG- codons, so a GS linker is GC-rich at positions 1-2 whatever
is done to position 3; FLAG's eight residues are too few to move a construct
and its Asp/Tyr/Lys composition restricts which third bases are even available.
Only the eGFP copies are long enough for the recoder to place freely.

Both are read from already-exported tables; nothing is recomputed from the
genome, so this notebook is fast.

# 1. Load Libraries

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(readxl)
library(Biostrings)

source(here("code", "cds_reporter_design", "reporter_helpers.R"))

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 5)

indir <- here("output", "cds_reporter_design")
```

# 2. The Recoded Parts

```{r read_recoded}
parts_csv <- file.path(indir,
               paste0("08_recoded_parts_", params$run_tag, ".csv"))
stopifnot("Recoded parts table not found: knit 08_ first" =
            file.exists(parts_csv))

GS_PART <- sprintf("GS linker (%dxGGGGS)", params$gs_repeats)

rec <- read_csv(parts_csv, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(part = str_remove(part, ",\\s*recoded$"))
stopifnot(
  "Recoded parts table is missing expected columns" =
    all(c("part", "nt", "gc_pct", "gc3_pct") %in% names(rec)),
  "Expected one GS linker, one FLAG part and at least one eGFP copy" =
    sum(rec$part == GS_PART) == 1 && sum(rec$part == "FLAG (1x)") == 1 &&
    sum(str_detect(rec$part, "^eGFP")) >= 1
)
print(rec %>% dplyr::select(-cds) %>%
        mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 1))) %>% as.data.frame())
```

# 3. The Same Parts Before Recoding

eGFP and FLAG come from the parts spreadsheet, so this notebook does not depend
on `08_` having exported them. Every eGFP copy starts from the same native
sequence, so the three "original" eGFP bars are by definition the same number -
the copies only diverge once they are recoded.

The GS linker is the exception: it has no spreadsheet row, so its "original" is
the naive encoding built from the exported 231 usage table. That is a tandem
repeat of one 15 nt unit, which is asserted here - it is the whole reason the
linker was recoded rather than ordered as written.

```{r read_originals}
parts_xlsx <- here("accessories", "cds seq.xlsx")
stopifnot("accessories/cds seq.xlsx not found" = file.exists(parts_xlsx))

ptb <- read_excel(parts_xlsx)
names(ptb)[1] <- "construct"
pseq <- ptb %>%
  filter(!is.na(construct), !is.na(cds)) %>%
  transmute(part = tolower(str_trim(construct)),
            seq  = toupper(gsub("\\s", "", cds)))
pseq <- setNames(pseq$seq, pseq$part)

egfp   <- pseq[["egfp"]]
flag1x <- substr(pseq[["flag3x"]], 43, 66)
stopifnot(
  "1xFLAG does not encode the DYKDDDDK epitope" =
    as.character(translate(DNAString(flag1x))) == "DYKDDDDK",
  "egfp is not 723 nt" = nchar(egfp) == 723
)

use_csv <- file.path(indir,
             paste0("08_codon_usage_231_", params$run_tag, ".csv"))
stopifnot("Codon usage table not found: knit 08_ first" = file.exists(use_csv))
usage    <- read_csv(use_csv, show_col_types = FALSE)
gs_aa    <- strrep("GGGGS", params$gs_repeats)
gs_naive <- naive_encoding(gs_aa, usage)
stopifnot(
  "The naive GS linker does not encode the GGGGS repeat" =
    as.character(translate(DNAString(gs_naive))) == gs_aa,
  "The naive GS linker is not an exact tandem repeat" =
    max_internal_repeat(gs_naive) >= nchar(gs_naive) - 15L
)

orig_of <- function(p)
  if (p == GS_PART) gs_naive else if (p == "FLAG (1x)") flag1x else egfp
orig <- rec %>%
  transmute(part,
            nt      = map_int(part, ~ nchar(orig_of(.x))),
            gc_pct  = map_dbl(part, ~ gc_pct_of(orig_of(.x))),
            gc3_pct = map_dbl(part, ~ compute_gc3_pct(orig_of(.x))))

stopifnot(
  "Recoding changed a part's length" = all(orig$nt == rec$nt),
  "Original and recoded GC3 are identical: nothing was recoded" =
    !isTRUE(all.equal(orig$gc3_pct, rec$gc3_pct))
)
print(orig %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 1))) %>%
        as.data.frame())
```

# 4. The Background Reference

```{r read_background}
med_csv <- file.path(indir, "01_group_medians_cds_gc.csv")
stopifnot("Background medians not found: knit 01_ first" = file.exists(med_csv))

meds <- read_csv(med_csv, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(group == "All expressed mRNAs")
stopifnot("Expected exactly one 'All expressed mRNAs' row" = nrow(meds) == 1)

BG_GC  <- meds$median_gc_pct
BG_GC3 <- meds$median_gc3_pct
cat("MDA-MB-231 expressed median - GC:", BG_GC, "% | GC3:", BG_GC3,
    "% (n =", format(meds$n, big.mark = ","), ")\n")
```

# 5. The Plots

```{r assemble}
bar_tbl <- bind_rows(orig %>% mutate(version = "Original"),
                     rec  %>% dplyr::select(part, nt, gc_pct, gc3_pct) %>%
                       mutate(version = "Recoded")) %>%
  mutate(part    = factor(part, levels = rec$part),
         version = factor(version, levels = c("Original", "Recoded")))

ver_cols <- c("Original" = "grey70", "Recoded" = "#0072B2")

bar_plot <- function(yvar, bg, ylab, title, caption) {
  ggplot(bar_tbl, aes(part, .data[[yvar]], fill = version)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.78), width = 0.72) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = bg, linetype = 2, color = "grey25") +
    annotate("text", x = 0.55, y = bg, vjust = -0.6, hjust = 0, size = 3.1,
             color = "grey25",
             label = paste0("MDA-MB-231 expressed median, ",
                            round(bg, 1), "%")) +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", .data[[yvar]])),
              position = position_dodge(width = 0.78),
              vjust = -0.45, size = 3.1, color = "grey20") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = ver_cols, name = NULL) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = ylab, title = title, caption = caption) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "top",
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1))
}
```

## GC content

```{r plot_gc}
p_gc <- bar_plot(
  "gc_pct", BG_GC, "GC (%)",
  "GC content of each part, before and after recoding",
  paste("Parts on their own, not the assembled constructs: the fixed",
        "HiBiT/P2A backbone\nand the linkers are excluded."))
print(p_gc)
ggsave(here("plots", paste0("cds_reporter_11_part_gc_", params$run_tag, ".pdf")),
       p_gc, width = 7.5, height = 5)
```

## GC3

```{r plot_gc3}
p_gc3 <- bar_plot(
  "gc3_pct", BG_GC3, "GC3 (%)",
  "GC3 of each part, before and after recoding",
  paste("The GS linker and FLAG sit low on purpose: both are inside the bare",
        "rung, whose fixed\nHiBiT and P2A are 31 of 54 codons at GC3 74%, so",
        "the 23 free codons spend themselves\npulling the rung as a whole down."))
print(p_gc3)
ggsave(here("plots", paste0("cds_reporter_11_part_gc3_", params$run_tag, ".pdf")),
       p_gc3, width = 7.5, height = 5)
```

# 6. What the Two Panels Say

```{r summary}
summ <- bar_tbl %>%
  dplyr::select(part, version, gc_pct, gc3_pct) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(gc_pct, gc3_pct), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = version, values_from = value) %>%
  mutate(metric = recode(metric, gc_pct = "GC", gc3_pct = "GC3"),
         target = if_else(metric == "GC", BG_GC, BG_GC3),
         delta  = Recoded - Original,
         miss   = Recoded - target) %>%
  arrange(metric, part)
print(summ %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 1))) %>%
        as.data.frame())
```

**The three eGFP copies are indistinguishable on GC3 and nearly so on GC.** All
three land on exactly the same GC3, because the recoder is given a third-base
*count* per block and the copies all get the same count; they differ in which
codons realise it, not in how many. The small GC difference between copies is
first- and second-base divergence in the Leu, Arg and Ser positions, which is
the composition-level trace of the fact that the copies are not a tandem repeat.

**Neither the GS linker nor FLAG is on target, and reading their bars as a miss
would be reading them wrong.** They are the two free parts of the bare rung,
and the recoder is given a third-base count for that rung as a whole, not for
each part: 31 of its 54 codons are the fixed HiBiT and P2A at GC3 74%, so the
23 free codons are spent pulling the *rung* onto the background and land well
below it themselves. The bare rung ends up within a point of the target
(`08_`); its parts individually do not, and were never asked to.

**The GS linker also cannot match on total GC, whatever happens at position 3.**
Every glycine codon is GG-, every serine codon TC- or AG-, so two thirds of the
linker's bases are set by the peptide. Its GC bar is high and its GC3 bar low
for the same reason, and the gap between them is the part of composition a
synonymous recode can never reach.

**FLAG is no longer driven to GC3 = 0%**, which it was before the GS linker
existed: with only 8 free codons in the rung, every one of them had to go to an
A/T-ending codon, and Asp, Tyr and Lys left no GC-ending option once that was
decided. The linker's 15 extra free codons absorb most of that burden, so FLAG
now keeps some GC-ending codons. The GC3 = 0% case is therefore no longer part
of this design - the README keeps the evidence that it would have been safe
anyway, since 51% of expressed MDA-MB-231 transcripts carry a run of 8
consecutive GC3 = 0% codons with no difference in riboseq TPM.

```{r checks}
# The recoding must move eGFP toward the background on GC3 and must not have
# moved it past the target by more than it started away from it.
egfp_rows <- summ %>% filter(metric == "GC3", str_detect(part, "^eGFP"))
stopifnot(
  "Recoding did not lower eGFP GC3" = all(egfp_rows$delta < 0),
  "Recoded eGFP GC3 is further from the target than the original was" =
    all(abs(egfp_rows$miss) < abs(egfp_rows$Original - egfp_rows$target))
)
cat("eGFP GC3 moved", round(mean(egfp_rows$Original), 1), "% ->",
    round(mean(egfp_rows$Recoded), 1), "% against a target of",
    round(BG_GC3, 1), "%\n")

# The GS linker and FLAG are expected to MISS, and saying so is the point: they
# are the bare rung's free codons, spent on the rung rather than on themselves.
# What is asserted is the direction - both recoded below target - not any
# magnitude, which depends on how the 23 free codons happen to split and would
# make this a check that fires on a legitimate redraw.
short_rows <- summ %>% filter(metric == "GC3", part %in% c(GS_PART, "FLAG (1x)"))
stopifnot(
  "Expected a GS linker and a FLAG row" = nrow(short_rows) == 2,
  "A short free part is not below the background GC3: it is absorbing no excess" =
    all(short_rows$Recoded < short_rows$target)
)
print(short_rows %>% dplyr::select(part, Original, Recoded, target, delta) %>%
        mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 1))) %>% as.data.frame())

# The GS linker's GC is high and its GC3 low because Gly and Ser fix positions
# 1-2. Asserting that pairing is what keeps the two panels from being read as
# contradicting each other.
gs_gc <- summ %>% filter(part == GS_PART)
stopifnot(
  "GS linker GC is not above background: positions 1-2 are not GG/TC as expected" =
    gs_gc$Recoded[gs_gc$metric == "GC"] > gs_gc$target[gs_gc$metric == "GC"],
  "GS linker GC3 is not below background" =
    gs_gc$Recoded[gs_gc$metric == "GC3"] < gs_gc$target[gs_gc$metric == "GC3"]
)
cat("GS linker: GC", round(gs_gc$Recoded[gs_gc$metric == "GC"], 1),
    "% (above background) but GC3",
    round(gs_gc$Recoded[gs_gc$metric == "GC3"], 1),
    "% (below) - Gly/Ser fix two bases in three\n")
```
